summary: An interior page of the Jamestown Weekly Alert for late September 1883, dense with multi-column editorial text and no display advertising. The page is divided across at least five columns and covers a wide range of subjects: a long leading editorial on North Dakota statehood and territorial politics, county commissioner proceedings, a 'Who Is He?' column on a local postmaster, a 'News by Telegraph' column of brief national and international dispatches, and a miscellany of local items including court dockets, road supervisor notices, and a billiards match brief. The editorial tone is engaged and opinionated, particularly on statehood and the conduct of public officials. Type is uniformly small with few visual breaks between items.

clipping_placements.placement_note: set as a brief paragraph within the county commissioner or local items column, mid-to-lower page, surrounded by similar short notices

juxtapositions: The billiards match brief at Murphy's saloon sits within a densely packed column of local legal and civic notices — road supervisor appointments and commissioner proceedings — giving the leisure item an incongruous bureaucratic neighbourhood.
